_meanings:
.²1 A medicinal climbing plant.
.²2 <ab>N.</ab> of the wife of Vasiṣṭha;

 {#anvAsitamarunDatyA svAhayeva havirBujam#} <ls>R. 1. 56</ls>.
.²3 The morning star personified as the wife of Vasiṣṭha; one of the Pleiades.
.²4 <ab>N.</ab> of the daughter of {#prAcetasadakza#}, one of the 10 wives of Dharma.
 [In mythology Arundhatī is represented as the wife of the sage Vasiṣṭha,
 one of the 7 sages. She was one of the 9 daughters of Kardama Prajāpati
 by Devahūti. She is regarded as the highest pattern of conjugal excellence
 and wifely devotion and is so invoked by the bridegroom at nuptial ceremonies.
 Though a woman she was regarded with the same, even more, veneration as
 the Saptarṣis; <ab>cf.</ab> <ls>Ku. 6. 12</ls>; {#tAmagOravaBedena munIMScApaSyadISvaraH .#}
 {#strI pumAnityanAsTEzA vfttaM hi mahitaM satAm ..#} <ab>cf.</ab> also Janakaʼs
 remarks in <ls>U. 4. 10</ls>. She, like her husband, was the guide and controller
 of Raghuʼs line in her own department and acted as guardian angel to Sītā
 after she had been abandoned by Rāma. It is said that Arundhatī (the
 star) is not seen by persons whose end has approached. <ab>cf.</ab> <ls>Suśr.</ls> {#na#}
 {#paSyati sanakzatrAM yastu devImarunDatIm . DruvamAkASagaNgAM ca taM vadanti#}
 {#gatAyuzam ..#}; see <ls>H. 1. 66</ls> also].
.²5 The tongue (personified).

<ab>N.</ab> of Vasiṣṭha one of the seven Ṛṣis
 or stars in the Ursa Major. {#-darSananyAyaH#} see under {#nyAya#}.
